newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt mart breaks record in 1st half.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt mart breaks record in 1st half.

text.p: The corporate bond sector for primary issuance saw a record-breaking first half with a total of $192 billion in straight debt priced in the public market, according to research firm Securities Data Co.

Not since the first half of 1993 had the market seen such heavy issuance of straight debt when a total of $162.3 billion was priced in the primary sector, said Richard Peterson, a spokesperson for Securities Data Co.
Another record was set in the private placement market where $27.4 billion in high-yield debt was issued. The figure exceeded 1996's second half high when $19.4 billion was sold.
In addition, the high-grade arena recorded a total $178.6 billion in new debt issuance for the first half of the year, beating the first half of 1996 when $142.4 billion was priced.
In the public sector, junk offerings dropped off to $13.1 billion versus $19.4 billion in the same period a year ago.
As high-yield debt dropped off in the public arena, private placements grew to comprise slightly above 50 percent of the market, according to Securities Data.
"Contrary to popular sentiment in the first quarter the market did not get trashed ... there were adjustments but the tone remained positive," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Aiding the bulk of new supply is an improved interest rate environment coupled with the improved credit quality of issuers, corporate bond participants said.
"The health of issuance suggests that investors feel comfortable with the current levels of interest rates," said John Lonski, economist at Moody's Investors Service Inc.
Lonski said the narrowing of spreads between corporates and U.S. Treasuries has spurred issuers to offer securities.
"Generally, the healthy state of credit quality helps to explain why spreads narrowed," Lonski said.
"That would include investor confidence in the adequacy of near-term earnings growth as far as maintaining the credit worth of corporate issuers," Lonski added.

Seperately, 144A private placement high-yield debt issues continue to grow in popularity, providing issuers with quick access to the corporate debt arena during a period of favorable rates, dealers said.

The key feature of the 144A private placement offering is the issuer's ability to accelerate the timing of the issue to take advantage of lower rates. The deal can be registered at a later point with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
